spotify.description: Tracks your current Spotify play state.
spotify.clientIdDescription: developer.spotify.com/dashboard → create an app → Redirect URI: http://127.0.0.1:47891/callback/spotify

twitch.description: Detects subscriptions, raids, and follows on your channel.
twitch.clientIdDescription: Optional: your own Client ID overrides the built-in one. dev.twitch.tv/console/apps → register an application → Redirect URI: http://localhost:47891/callback/twitch

windowsMedia.title: Windows Media
windowsMedia.description: Shows the current track from whatever player is running on your PC — Spotify, a browser tab, VLC, and more. No auth needed. Windows only.
windowsMedia.enableDescription: Polls the system media session every few seconds while enabled

youtube.description: Detects memberships and Super Chats on your stream.
youtube.clientSecretDescription: Google issues a secret for Desktop apps too — it's needed to exchange the code for a token

random.title: Random
random.description: A random number generator with a hash shown below it — viewers can verify the result wasn't changed after it was announced.
random.verifyHint: The hash is published right away. Number = min + (first 4 bytes of SHA-256(seed + ":" + index)) % (max − min + 1), index starting from 0. Once the seed is revealed, anyone can verify fairness.
random.waitingReveal: Hash published. Click "Reveal result" when you're ready.

roulette.title: Roulette
roulette.description: A wheel with a countdown — viewers join it with a chat command or by redeeming a channel points reward.
roulette.commandHint: A viewer's message matching this text (case-insensitive) enters them into the current round.
roulette.pointsRewardHint: The reward list is pulled from Twitch — connect the Twitch integration and create a reward in your creator dashboard.
roulette.pointsStackHint: Each repeat redemption of the reward gives that viewer one more ticket — their odds of winning grow proportionally with how many times they redeem.
roulette.entryModeHintFollowers: Both the chat command and the points reward will only accept entries from channel followers.
roulette.entryModeHintSubscribers: Both the chat command and the points reward will only accept entries from channel subscribers.
roulette.helpDescription: SHA-256(seed) is published the moment the round starts — before anyone could enter. The seed is revealed as soon as entries close, so anyone can recompute the hash and re-run the draw themselves.
roulette.helpFormula:
roll = parseInt(SHA-256(seed).slice(0, 8), 16) % totalWeight
winner = first entrant (in join order) whose running weight total > roll

welcome.title: Welcome to OBScure
welcome.description: This is your control panel for OBS overlays, on-stream tools like Random and Roulette, and service integrations. Let's walk through the main sections — it'll take less than a minute.

sidebarNav.title: Navigation
sidebarNav.description: This is where you switch between sections: Dashboard, Overlays, Tools, Integrations, and Settings.

dashboardIntegrations.title: Integration status
dashboardIntegrations.description: The dashboard shows which services are connected — active ones are highlighted in green.

integrationsConnect.title: Connecting a service
integrationsConnect.description: The integration pages connect Spotify, Twitch, and YouTube — usually just one button and a browser confirmation.

settingsOverlayAddress.title: Overlay server address
settingsOverlayAddress.description: Host and port of the local server that serves overlays for OBS. Shared by every overlay.

settingsCanvas.title: Canvas
settingsCanvas.description: The stream's resolution and aspect ratio — only affects how the overlay previews look here in the app.

restartTour.title: The walkthrough is always here
restartTour.description: Want to go through it again? This button restarts it from the beginning. That's it — happy streaming!

sceneBuilderWelcome.title: Scene Builder
sceneBuilderWelcome.description: Every scene here is one node graph that becomes one Browser Source page for OBS. Let's walk through the core mechanics in detail — a couple of minutes.

sceneBuilderAddNode.title: Adding nodes
sceneBuilderAddNode.description: Click a group to expand it, then a node to drop it on the canvas. A group's color matches the node's own color once it's placed.

sceneBuilderWiring.title: Wiring nodes together
sceneBuilderWiring.description: Drag from the dot on a node's right to a socket on another node's left. The socket's color shows its type: green — content (Text/Image/Video/Shape), amber — a style modifier, sky blue — data, indigo — process sequence. Something only renders once it reaches the Scene node.

sceneBuilderModifiers.title: Modifiers
sceneBuilderModifiers.description: Position, Size, Opacity, Shadow and others are separate nodes wired INTO whatever they affect, not the other way around. Many nodes have a "?" next to their title — that's where the extra detail lives when the node's own fields aren't enough.

sceneBuilderPreview.title: Preview
sceneBuilderPreview.description: Shows how the scene will look in OBS, matching the real canvas resolution. The ▶ button plays animations and sound locally — no real event needed.

sceneBuilderSaveTest.title: Save vs. Test
sceneBuilderSaveTest.description: Save persists silently — no replayed animations or Background FX. Test pushes the current (even unsaved) graph to a real Browser Source and replays the entrance — handy for checking before you commit to Save.

sceneBuilderUrl.title: The OBS link
sceneBuilderUrl.description: This address is the Browser Source itself — copy it into OBS. It updates the moment the URL key changes.

sceneBuilderPatterns.title: Three scene modes
sceneBuilderPatterns.description: Static — always on screen. Event-triggered (Event + Timer → Scene) — shows for a fixed duration when an alert fires. Process (Start → Task → Wait → End) — a step-by-step sequence with precise timing and its own animation per step. That's it — happy building!

nav.prettify: Prettify — auto-arranges the node graph for readability. Only rearranges nodes locally; Save to keep it.

tooltip.notWired: Not wired into rendering yet — this node can be placed and connected, but currently has no effect on the overlay.
tooltip.priority: Render priority {position} of {total} — click to move to end, right-click to set a specific position
tooltip.backgroundFxLoop: Off (default): drops it once — use Play/Test to replay it. On: keeps dropping one at a time for as long as the scene is showing.

nodes.group: An invisible wrapper with no background, padding, or border — wire in other Content nodes to move or arrange them as one unit.
nodes.randomPick: Shows exactly ONE of its wired Options each time the scene shows — picked fresh on every replay. Equal odds by default; check Custom chance to weight them (0 excludes an option entirely). Carries no size/position of its own — the picked Option keeps its own wiring untouched.
nodes.audioPlayer: Live now-playing data from Spotify or Windows Media. Check each output's own help for exactly where to wire it.
nodes.randomSource: Live commit/reveal state from the Random tool, auto-paired with its own display widget. Check each output's own help for where to wire it.
nodes.rouletteEntrants: Formats its paired Roulette's entrants into rows — wire the output into another node's Content socket to display them, its own styling still applies. Unlike its paired display widget, this one can be deleted freely.
nodes.randomWidget: Shows the rolling numbers, always paired 1:1 with its own source node and visible by default. Wire that source's Event output into this node's Visibility socket to hide it outside an active roll.
nodes.rouletteWidget: The spinning wheel, always paired 1:1 with its own source node and visible by default. Wire that source's Event output into this node's Visibility socket to hide it outside an active round.
nodes.rouletteSource: Live entrants and round phase from the Roulette tool, auto-paired with its own display widget. Check each output's own help for where to wire it.
nodes.start: Entry point for the process — wire in a Live Data-section trigger to say what starts it.
nodes.task: Wire in the Target this step acts on, plus any modifiers. A sound cue also needs a Target wired — even an otherwise-inert Update step — since that's what anchors it to this moment.
nodes.condition: Branches the process in two: Then fires when Field/Is/Value matches this alert, Else otherwise. Only meaningful for a process armed by a real Event — one armed by Audio Player/Roulette/Random has no alert to check, so it always falls to Else, same as a Field simply absent from this alert (Amount on a follow, say).
nodes.image: Leave URL empty to show the live now-playing album art, or wire a Live Data-section node's Content output into Content for the same result, explicitly (the URL field goes read-only). Defaults to 96×96 — wire in a Transform-section node to override the size.
nodes.video: Defaults to 320×180 — wire in a Transform-section node to override the size.
nodes.videoAutoplay: Off relies on the browser allowing autoplay audio, which isn't guaranteed — pair with an Effects-section node for reliable sound instead.
nodes.scene: The output — only what's wired in here is rendered.
nodes.end: Exit point — the process finishes and the scene clears here.

outputs.structural: Makes this part of what's actually rendered — wire it into a Content-section container's Children socket to nest it, or straight into the top-level Content socket to place it directly.
outputs.target: Wire into a Process-section step's Target socket to mark this as what that step shows, hides, or updates. This doesn't replace the Structural wire — a component still needs that too, or it won't render at all.
outputs.caption: Wire into an Effects-section effect's own Caption socket to caption its drop with this text.
outputs.audioContent: Bundles Artist, Title, and Cover in one wire. Wire it into a Content-section node's own Content socket — which fields apply depends on where it lands.
outputs.audioEvent: The track-change/now-playing signal. Wire into a Process-section entry point to arm it on track change, and/or into the scene-level Event socket to show or hide the whole scene by playback state — both at once is fine.
outputs.rouletteContent: Feeds this node's own paired display widget and entrant list through their shared Source socket — that's all it's for. The widget's link is permanent, the entrant list's isn't.
outputs.rouletteEvent: The round's phase signal. Wire into a Process-section entry point to arm it the moment a round starts, or into the paired widget's Visibility socket to hide it outside an active round — both at once is fine.
outputs.rouletteEntrantsContent: Wire into a Content-section node's own Content socket to replace its template with this list's formatted rows — that node's own text field goes read-only while connected. Its styling fields stay its own; only row formatting lives here.
outputs.randomContent: Wire into this node's own paired display widget's Source socket (a permanent pairing), or into any Content-section node's own Content socket to fill its placeholders — the template stays editable.
outputs.randomEvent: The roll's phase signal. Wire into a Process-section entry point to arm it the moment a roll is committed, or into the paired widget's Visibility socket to hide it outside an active roll — both at once is fine.
outputs.conditionThen: Wire into the next step to take when this Condition matches. Same Event socket every other process step uses (Task/Wait/Condition/End).
outputs.conditionElse: Wire into the next step to take when this Condition does NOT match — including whenever there's no real alert to check at all (an Audio Player/Roulette/Random-armed process, or a missing Field).
